title: Multitenant Impact Assessment Playbook and Customer Notice Templates
author: Lena M. Ortega
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a standardized process for assessing, communicating, and resolving incidents that have multitenant impact on Redwood Inference (partial or full affecting multiple customers). It combines an operational decision ladder, a reproducible tenant-impact assessment checklist, template messages for customer notifications and the status page, and a short training exercise you can run during game days. The goal is fast, accurate assessment and customer-safe messaging that preserves trust while giving engineering and support teams a clear restoration path.

Scope and audience

- Scope: incidents that affect more than one tenant (≥2 distinct customers), including: noisy neighbors, degradation of embeddings/kv-cache, routing misconfiguration, cross-tenant quota enforcement bugs, region-level capacity saturation.
- Audience: oncall engineers, bridge operators, SRE leads, customer success (CSRs) and account managers who will draft customer notices.

Goals

1. Produce a defensible impact assessment within 15 minutes of reliable detection.
2. Publish an initial customer-facing status update within 30 minutes for Severity >= S2 multitenant impact.
3. Provide tailored remediation pipelines (isolate, throttle, rollback, region-failover) mapped to impact level and tenant-criticality.

Definitions and severity mapping (multitenant-specific)

| Severity | Symptoms (multitenant) | Target response SLA | Customer notice? | Typical action 
|---|---|---:|:--:|---|
| S1 (Critical) | Majority of requests for multiple tenants failing (errors >= 50% p95), billing-impacting, SLAs breached | 15 min acknowledge, immediate bridge | Yes (all affected tenants) | Rollforward/rollback, emergency capacity reassign
| S2 (High) | Significant latency (p95 > 2x baseline) or partial functional regressions across tenants | 30 min acknowledge, 1 hr mitigation plan | Yes (affected tenants + broad notice) | Traffic shaping, throttle noisy tenants, region swap
| S3 (Medium) | Reduced performance limited to subset of tenants, non-critical features affected | 1 hr ack, 24h remediation | Yes (affected tenants) | QoS config, autoscale, patching window
| S4 (Low) | Single-tenant root cause with transient bleed across others (<2% of requests) | 4 hr ack | Optional | Follow-up fix, monitoring tune

Roles & responsibilities

- First Responder (FR): owner of immediate mitigation steps (usually oncall engineer). Responsible for impact report and initial status draft.
- Bridge Operator (BO): runs the incident bridge, coordinates comms cadence.
- Service Steward: long-term owner for the affected service, drives root cause, fixes and rollouts.
- CS Liaison: summarizes tenant-level impact and orchestrates customer-specific outreach.
- SRE Lead: approves high-risk mitigations (capacity rebalancing, cross-region failover).

Fast tenant-impact assessment (15-minute checklist)

1. Data sources to query immediately (order matters):
   - Metrics: service p50/p95/p999 latency and error-rate by tenant id (from Observability dashboard).
   - Logs: recent 15m error spikes correlated with model variants or host pools.
   - Routing/Config: recent routing policy or deploy changes in last 60 minutes.
   - Quota/Rate-limit: token/embedding quota enforcement logs.
   - Capacity: GPU pool utilization and pending queue length.
2. Execute quick queries (examples):
   - Internal metrics API (replace with appropriate token):
     curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN\" \"https://internal-metrics.redwood/v1/tenant-aggregate?service=serving&window=15m\" | jq .
   - Find top-10 tenants by error increase (Postgres example):
     SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS errors, SUM(requests) FROM request_events 
       WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes'
       GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 10;
3. Produce a single-line impact summary: e.g. \"Impact: ~12 tenants (top 3: tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c) experiencing 60% error rate on text-generation in us-west-2; likely noisy neighbor on dedicated pool B.\"
4. Flag customer-critical tenants (from CS roster) for immediate one-to-one outreach.

Decision ladder and common remediation patterns

1. Throttle/Rate-limit noisy tenants (low risk): quick, reversible, preserves availability.
2. Isolate noisy tenant traffic to separate pool (medium risk): needs coordination with infra and CS.
3. Fallback to smaller/cheaper model variants (medium risk): reduces compute pressure, may affect quality.
4. Region failover (high risk): requires SRE Lead approval and careful customer notice.
5. Emergency rollback of recent deploy (high risk): if correlation points to deployment.

Sample impact assessment template (single paragraph for bridge and status page)

\"Brief: Between 13:04–13:18 UTC we observed a sustained increase in errors affecting ~10 tenants using text-generation in us-west-2. Error-rate reached 55% p95. Initial indicators point to a resource contention event in GPU pool pool-b-3. FR has isolated pool and enabled per-tenant throttling; mitigation in progress. Next update in 30 min.\"

Customer notice templates

(1) Initial short notice (S1/S2, sent within 30 minutes)

Subject: Service interruption impacting some customers – Redwood Inference

Body: 
Hi <Customer Name>,

We are investigating an operational issue affecting inference traffic in us-west-2 that may impact your requests. Our oncall team has identified elevated error rates and is actively working on mitigation. We will follow up with an update within 30 minutes. You can track public updates here: <status.redwood.example/incident-id>.

If your workload is mission-critical and you would like immediate manual assistance (workarounds or priority routing), reply to this message and we will coordinate a temporary mitigation.

— Redwood Inference Support

(2) Technical update (30–90 minutes)

Subject: Technical update — mitigation in progress for inference errors in us-west-2

Body: 
Details: We have applied per-tenant rate limiting for the top noisy customers and rebalanced traffic away from GPU pool pool-b-3. Error rates have fallen from 55% to 12% for most tenants; a small subset is still experiencing elevated latency.
Action required: None at this time. If you continue to see impact, please share a sample request-id and timestamp.
Next update: 60 minutes or when status changes.

(3) Resolution notice (S1/S2)

Subject: Resolved — inference service restored in us-west-2

Body: 
We have fully restored service for the affected tenants. Root cause: resource contention in pool-b-3 caused by a noisy model variant on dedicated capacity. Fix: temporary throttles removed; noisy tenant isolated to its own pool; long-term fix scheduled (rollout of throttling-by-default and autoscale tuning). If you experienced billing errors or suspect data loss, open a support ticket referencing incident ID <INC-YYYYMMDD-###>.

Status page messaging (initial/update/resolved)

- Initial status page snippet (use for public page):
  Title: Degraded inference performance in us-west-2 – under investigation
  Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors or latency.
  Next update: 30 minutes.

- Update (intermediate):
  Title: Mitigation in progress — traffic rebalanced and throttles applied
  Details: Error rates reduced but some tenants still affected; targeted mitigation continues.

- Resolved:
  Title: Incident resolved — service operating normally
  Details: Full restoration completed at 14:12 UTC. Postmortem in progress.

Escalation scripts and recommended phrasing for sensitive accounts

When contacting enterprise/key accounts, include:
- A clear acknowledgement of impact (what failed, approximate window, how it affected their SLA).
- Concrete steps taken immediately to protect the tenant (e.g., isolated to separate pool, manual reroute).
- Next steps and owner for follow-up.

Example short script for CS outreach (phone/email):
\"Hi <Name>, this is <Engineer/CSR>. We detected increased failures affecting your inference requests between 13:04–13:18 UTC. We’ve isolated your traffic to a dedicated pool and applied rate-limits to protect throughput while we stabilize the cluster. I will keep you updated and we have a support ticket opened (ID: <ticket>). Do you have any urgent queries or a hard cutoff we should be aware of?\"

For very sensitive customers (contractual SLAs), always copy the SRE Lead and the account executive in the first notice.

Quiet-window guidance and scheduling

- Quiet window definition: a scheduled period (usually 30–120 minutes) during which non-essential changes and noisy introductions (model variant swaps, heavy retraining) are paused for affected services.
- When to enact: after an S2/S1 incident once mitigation is active and until confidence threshold reached (p95 error < baseline * 1.2 for 2 continuous 15m windows).
- How to announce internally: create a short incident notice in #incident-ops channel with tags: #quiet-window, include duration, FR, BO, and service steward.

Runbook references and commands

- Quick runbook IDs:
  - RB-ISOLATE-01: Per-tenant throttling and pool isolation (runbook)
  - RB-ROLL-DEPLOY-02: Emergency rollback and controlled reroute
  - RB-REGION-FAILOVER-03: Cross-region routing and DNS switch
- Useful commands (examples):
  - Isolate tenant: internal-cli routes isolate --tenant tenant-id --pool pool-id --reason \"noisy-neighbor\"
  - Apply throttle: internal-cli throttle apply --tenant tenant-id --qps 0.5
  - Rebalance GPU pool: infra-cmd pool rebalance --pool pool-b-3 --target pool-b-4

Post-incident actions (first 72 hours)

1. Immediate: confirm all mitigations reverted (if temporary) and verify metric baselines.
2. Within 24 hours: publish a technical postmortem draft with impact table (affected-tenants, minutes of degraded service, remediation steps taken).
3. Within 72 hours: finalize RCA, mitigation plan, and timeline for permanent fixes (autoscale tuning, default throttles, improved tenant isolation).
4. Notify affected tenants individually if they require credits or compensation; coordinate with finance/legal for policy compliance.

Game day exercise (30–60 minute lab)

Objective: practice producing a 15-minute impact assessment and a 30-minute customer notice for a simulated noisy-tenant causing multitenant degradation.

Exercise steps:
- Pre-brief (5 min): assign roles (FR, BO, Service Steward, CS Liaison).
- Simulation (20 min): inject synthetic errors into a test pool, run the quick queries and draft initial status and one customer notice.
- Debrief (15–35 min): review timing, clarity of messages, and decision whether to throttle or isolate. Capture improvements for runbook RB-ISOLATE-01.

Measurement and SLO checks

- Use this playbook in conjunction with core SLOs: request-success-rate >= 99.7% p95 and latency p95 <= configured baseline per model.
- Evidence required for postmortem: raw metric graphs, tenant-impact table export CSV, list of commands executed (audit log ID), and status page timeline.

Attachments and artifacts to include in postmortem

- Tenants-impacted.csv (columns: tenant_id, org_name, start_ts, end_ts, p95_error_rate, manual_actions)
- Commands-executed.log (audit IDs)
- Bridge-transcript.txt
- Status-page-snapshots (initial, update, resolved)

Governance and continuous improvement

- Every multitenant incident triggers a postmortem review with Platform, Serving Runtime, and CS representatives. Action items must be tracked in the incident board and assigned to a Service Steward within 48 hours.
- Quarterly game days should include one multitenant noisy-neighbor scenario to test throttling and isolation playbooks.
